questions.question:
Age of 6 boys A, B, C, D, E and F is compared. Age of no two boys is same. No one is elder than A. C is elder than D but younger than B. D is elder than E. F is younger than E.

Age of how many boys are less than D?
questions.solution:
Based on the information provided, we can determine the relative ages of the six boys:

1. ‘No one is elder than A’: Since no two boys have the same age, this means **A** is the eldest boy among the group. So, **A** > all others.

2. ‘C is elder than D but younger than B’: This gives us the sequence **B > C > D**.

3. ‘D is elder than E’ and ‘F is younger than E’: This establishes the sequence **D > E > F**.

Combining all these constraints into a single descending chain of ages, we get:

**A > B > C > D > E > F**

Now, we need to find the number of boys whose ages are less than **D**. From the sequence above, the boys younger than **D** are:

1. **E**

2. **F**

There are exactly **2** boys whose ages are less than **D**.

Hence, the correct answer is **‘Option 2’**.

questions.question: How much time (in minutes) (approximately) after 7:00 AM will it take for the minute and hour hands of the clock to be at an angle of 95 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360 ÷ 12 = 30°

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 30° ÷ 60 = 0.5°

The **minute hand** covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 360 ÷ 60 = 6°

The **relative speed** of the minute hand with respect to the hour hand = 6° − 0.5° = 5.5° per minute.

__**Calculation:**__

At **7:00 AM**, the hour hand is at 7 × 30° = 210° and the minute hand is at 0°.

Initial angle between the hands = 210° − 0° = 210°

To reach an angle of **95°**, the minute hand must cover a relative angular distance of:

Distance = 210° − 95° = 115°

Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time taken = 115 ÷ 5.5 = 230 ÷ 11 ≈ 20.909 minutes

The approximate time after **7:00 AM** is **21 minutes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by the formula:

Angle = | (60H - 11M)/(2) | 

Where **H** = hours and **M** = minutes.

Given **H = 7** and Angle = **95°**:

95 = | (60 times 7 - 11M)/(2) | 

190 = |420 − 11M|

For the first occurrence (before the minute hand passes the hour hand):

11M = 420 − 190

11M = 230

M = 230 ÷ 11 ≈ 20.909 minutes

Hence, the approximate time is **21 minutes**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **21**.

questions.question: A clock shows the correct time at 8 AM. The clock gains 2 seconds every 6 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 5 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

To find the time shown by the clock, we calculate the **total duration** elapsed and multiply it by the **rate of gain** of the clock.

**Total Duration** = Target Time − Initial Time

**Total Gain** = Total Duration × Rate of Gain per unit time

__Calculation:__

The clock gains **2 seconds every 6 minutes**.

Gain in 1 hour (60 minutes) = (60 / 6) × 2 seconds

Gain in 1 hour = 10 × 2 = **20 seconds**

Now, calculate the total time elapsed from **8 AM to 5 PM**:

From 8 AM to 12 PM (Noon) = 4 hours

From 12 PM to 5 PM = 5 hours

Total duration = 4 + 5 = **9 hours**

Total gain in 9 hours = 9 × 20 seconds = **180 seconds**

Convert the total gain from seconds to minutes:

Gain in minutes = 180 / 60 = **3 minutes**

The actual time is 5 PM. Since the clock is gaining time, it will show:

Clock Time = Actual Time + Gain

Clock Time = 5:00 PM + 3 minutes = **5:03 PM**

Hence, the correct answer is **5:03**.

questions.question: The Sundarbans are famous for which type of natural vegetation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mangrove forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sundarbans** constitute the largest contiguous **mangrove forest** ecosystem in the world, covering approximately 10,000 square kilometers across **India** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• Located at the mouth of the **Ganges**, **Brahmaputra**, and **Meghna** rivers on the **Bay of Bengal**, this region is a complex network of tidal waterways, mudflats, and small islands.
 
• The vegetation is dominated by **halophytes**, which are salt-tolerant plant species adapted to survive in harsh **intertidal zones** and saline soil conditions.
 
• The forest is named after the **Sundari tree** (**Heritiera fomes**), which provides high-quality timber and is the most abundant tree species in the area.
 
• Plants in this ecosystem feature specialized adaptations such as **pneumatophores** (breathing roots) that grow vertically upwards to facilitate gas exchange in **anaerobic** waterlogged soil.
 
• The **Sundarbans** is designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and a **Ramsar Site**, serving as a critical habitat for the endangered **Royal Bengal Tiger**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Evergreen Forests**:

 
 
• These occur in regions with more than **200 cm** of annual rainfall and temperatures between **25°C to 27°C**.
 
• Commonly found in the **Western Ghats**, **Northeast India**, and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.
 
 
 
• **Desert Vegetation**:
 
 
• Consists of **xerophytic** plants like cacti and thorny bushes found in **arid** regions with less than **50 cm** of rainfall, primarily in **Rajasthan** and **Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Alpine Meadows**:
 
 
• These are found in the high-altitude regions of the **Himalayas**, generally above **3,000 meters**, characterized by short grasses and **mosses**.

questions.question: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) requires completion of investigation in sexual offenses within:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 months**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**, which replaced the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)**, mandates a strict timeline for the completion of investigations in cases of **sexual offenses**.
 
• Under **Section 193(1)** of the **BNSS**, the investigation into offenses relating to **rape** and **sexual assault** must be completed within a period of **two months**.
 
• This specific timeframe applies to offenses defined under **Sections 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, and 79** of the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**.
 
• The **two-month period** is calculated from the date on which the **information** (FIR) was first recorded by the **officer-in-charge** of the police station.
 
• This provision ensures **expeditious justice** for survivors of sexual violence by preventing procedural delays at the **investigative stage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medical Examination:**

 
 
• According to **Section 184** of the **BNSS**, the **medical examination** of a victim of a sexual offense must be performed by a **Registered Medical Practitioner** within **24 hours** of the police receiving information about the crime.
 
 
 
• **Victim Rights and Updates:**
 
 
• The **BNSS** emphasizes **victim-centric justice**, requiring police to provide updates on the **progress of the investigation** to the victim or informant within **90 days**.
 
 
 
• **Effective Date:**
 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita**, along with the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** and the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam**, came into official force across India on **July 1, 2024**.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Supervision:**
 
 
• The **Magistrate** is empowered to monitor the investigation to ensure compliance with these **statutory timelines**, fostering greater **accountability** within the law enforcement agencies.

questions.question: Which of the following tax was levied on cultivation under the administration of Alauddin Khalji?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kharaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khalji** (1296−1316) introduced comprehensive agrarian reforms to maximize state revenue and maintain a powerful **standing army**.
 
• **Kharaj** was the specific agricultural land tax levied on the produce of the soil, which formed the backbone of the Sultanate's economy.
 
• Under his reign, the **Kharaj** was increased to **50 percent** of the total produce, representing the highest tax rate imposed by any Delhi Sultan.
 
• He implemented a system of **land measurement** known as **Masahat**, ensuring that tax was calculated based on the actual area under cultivation using the **Biswa** as a standard unit.
 
• To prevent local intermediaries like **Khuts** and **Muqaddams** from exploiting peasants or evading taxes, he abolished their traditional privileges and brought them under the same tax regime as ordinary cultivators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahzar**:

 
 
• It refers to a **formal petition** or a public attestation; most famously, the **Infallibility Decree** of **1579**.
 
• This decree was issued by the Mughal Emperor **Akbar** to establish his supremacy over the **Ulema** in matters of religious interpretation.
 
 
 
• **Amil**:
 
 
• A high-ranking **revenue official** responsible for the assessment and collection of taxes at the **Pargana** level.
 
• They were instrumental in documenting **cultivation patterns** and ensuring that the revenue reached the central treasury.
 
 
 
• **Other Taxes under Alauddin Khalji**:
 
 
• **Ghari**: A specialized tax imposed on the **residential houses** of the subjects.
 
• **Chari**: A **grazing tax** levied on the pasturage of milch animals and cattle.
 
• **Zakat**: A **religious tax** paid by Muslims, typically 2.5 percent of their total wealth, used for charitable purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from United States of America?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution is a borrowed feature from the **United States of America**, which was the first nation in the world to begin its constitution with a preamble.
 
• The phrase **'We, the People of India'** is directly inspired by the opening words of the **US Constitution**, which reads **'We, the People of the United States'**, signifying that power resides in the citizens.
 
• The Preamble serves as an introduction to the **Constitution of India**, outlining the fundamental values, philosophy, and objectives such as **Sovereignty, Socialism, Secularism, Democracy,** and **Republic**.
 
• Other significant features adopted from the **USA** include **Fundamental Rights**, the **Independence of the Judiciary**, **Judicial Review**, the **Impeachment of the President**, and the **Removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges**.

• **Fundamental Duties**:

 
 
• These were not part of the original constitution but were added via the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** based on the **Swaran Singh Committee** recommendations.
 
• The concept was borrowed from the constitution of the **USSR** (present-day Russia).
 
 
 
• **Concept of Republic**:
 
 
• The ideals of **Republic** and the principles of **Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity** in the Preamble were borrowed from the **French Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Freedom of Trade and Commerce**:
 
 
• Provisions relating to the **Freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse** (Article 301 to 307) and the concept of a **Joint Sitting of the two Houses of Parliament** were inspired by the **Australian Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**:
 
 
• The **DPSP** (Articles 36-51), which guide the state in making laws for social and economic justice, were borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.

__
 
• In **1875**, **Dwarkanath Ghose** revolutionized the musical instrument industry in India by designing a modified version of the **Harmonium** in **Calcutta** (modern-day **Kolkata**).
 
• Ghose was the founder of the renowned firm **Dwarkin & Son**, a name derived as a portmanteau of **Dwarkanath** and his son.
 
• The original **European harmonium** or **reed organ** was designed to be played with **foot-pedals** to pump air, which was physically incompatible with the traditional **Indian seating posture** where musicians sit on the floor (**Asana**).
 
• Dwarkanath Ghose adapted the instrument by replacing the foot-pedals with **hand-operated bellows** located at the back or front of the instrument, allowing the player to pump air with one hand while playing the **keyboard** with the other.
 
• This innovation made the instrument highly **portable**, easy to handle, and robust enough to withstand the **tropical climate** of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The **hand-pumped harmonium** quickly became an essential accompaniment for **vocal music**, providing a steady **drone** and melodic support across various genres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a **free-reed instrument** that generates sound as air flows past vibrating pieces of thin metal in a frame.
 
• Despite its **Western origins**, it is now deeply embedded in **Hindustani classical**, **Sufi** (such as **Qawwali**), and **devotional music** like **Bhajans** and **Kirtans**.
 
• The instrument was once banned from **All India Radio** (from 1940 to 1971) because purists argued it could not produce **Meend** (glissando) or the **Shrutis** (microtones) essential to **Indian Ragas**.
 
• Key components include the **bellows**, **air chamber**, **reeds** (often made of **brass** or **copper**), and the **keyboard** consisting of keys representing a **tempered scale**.

questions.question: 8 men can finish the work in 18 days, working 6 hours per day. How many men are required to finish the same work in 12 days, if each works 8 hours per day?

Use the **MDH** formula for work equality: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

864 = M₂ × 96

M₂ = 864 ÷ 96 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

Initial workforce (M₁) = **8 men**

Initial days (D₁) = **18 days**

Initial hours (H₁) = **6 hr per day**

Target days (D₂) = **12 days**

Target hours (H₂) = **8 hr per day**

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Men × Days × Hours

Since the **work is the same** in both cases: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e4a3ac47978ca3fbead9c61b45878e60f703d1f0dde44de95747060d65775c6.png]

⇒ Total work in man-hours = 8 × 18 × 6

⇒ 864 = M₂ × 12 × 8

⇒ 864 = M₂ × 96

⇒ M₂ = 864 ÷ 96

⇒ M₂ = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The MDH Rule

For any work involving men, days, and hours, the relation is (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂, where W represents the amount of work.

Inverse Proportion in Time & Work

The number of men is inversely proportional to the number of days and hours. If you double the men, the time required is halved for the same amount of work.

If individuals have different efficiencies (E), the formula expands to M₁×D₁×H₁×E₁ = M₂×D₂×H₂×E₂.

questions.question: The average of 24 numbers is 54. A number 'M' is subtracted from each number. New average of these 24 numbers is 42. What is the value of 'M'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a **constant value** is subtracted from every observation in a set, the **original average** also decreases by the **same value**.

New Average = Original Average − Value Subtracted (M)

42 = 54 − M

M = 54 − 42 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers in the set = **24**

Original Average = **54**

New Average after subtracting **M** from each = **42**

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

Property: If xᵢ → xᵢ − M, then Averageₙₑw = Averageₒₗd − M

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76dee8b5863ff4f1e613dc560a8456f4fcebf70d39ed3da08f3137810f84f772.png] 

⇒ Original Total Sum = 24 × 54 = 1296

⇒ New Total Sum = 24 × 42 = 1008

⇒ Total decrease in sum = 1296 − 1008 = 288

⇒ Since **M** was subtracted from each of the **24 numbers**, the total decrease = 24 × M

⇒ 24 × M = 288

⇒ M = 288 ÷ 24

⇒ M = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition Property

If a constant **k** is added to every number in a data set, the new average is **Original Average + k**.

Multiplication Property

If every number in a data set is multiplied by **k**, the new average is **Original Average × k**.

Division Property

If every number in a data set is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the new average is **Original Average ÷ k**.

questions.question: Average marks obtained by 20 boys is 44 (Each boy has obtained distinct value of marks). If the highest marks and lowest marks obtained are removed, then the average reduces by 4. What is the average of the highest and lowest marks obtained?

**Average of removed items** = Original Average + (Total Decrease in remaining sum ÷ Number of removed items)

Total decrease in sum of 18 boys = 18 × 4 = 72

Average of Highest and Lowest = 44 + (72 ÷ 2)

Average = 44 + 36 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial **average marks** (A₁) = 44

New number of **boys** (n₂) = 18 (after removing Highest and Lowest marks)

New **average marks** (A₂) = 44 − 4 = 40

**Formula:**

Total Marks = Average × Number of students

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1062b2f71905c678895a027e04291d4ba8c24c724fc7e9c6aa3c0fb49254051c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of **Highest (H)** and **Lowest (L)** marks = 880 − 720 = 160

⇒ Average of Highest and Lowest marks = 160 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

Exclusion Concept in Averages

When items are removed and the average decreases, the sum of removed items is greater than the original average share. Sum of excluded items = (Number of excluded items × Old Average) + (New Count × Decrease in Average).

Average of Group

The arithmetic mean or average is defined as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Average = (x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ) ÷ n.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Total Number of Factors

Number of Even Factors

questions.question: Which is the largest number that divides 91, 127, 199 and 235 to leave the same remainder in each case?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **largest number** that leaves the **same remainder**, calculate the **differences** between the numbers.

Differences are: (127 − 91) = 36; (199 − 127) = 72; (235 − 199) = 36.

The required number is the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of 36, 72, and 36.

HCF(36, 72, 36) = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 91, 127, 199, and 235.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = **HCF** of (|N₂ − N₁|, |N₃ − N₂|, |N₄ − N₃|)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20b3fe6c8a7d5fc0e4ffab81781388d2c3ff88a11ef117b33a157fc2ba375fca.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First difference = 127 − 91 = 36

⇒ Second difference = 199 − 127 = 72

⇒ Third difference = 235 − 199 = 36

⇒ Prime factorization of 36 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ **HCF** = 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36

⇒ Verify: 91 ÷ 36 = 2 (rem. 19), 127 ÷ 36 = 3 (rem. 19), 199 ÷ 36 = 5 (rem. 19), 235 ÷ 36 = 6 (rem. 19).

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the **greatest divisor** that exactly divides two or more numbers. For "same remainder" problems, always find the **HCF of the differences** between numbers.

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest number which is **exactly divisible** by each of the given numbers. Relationship: Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM.

Divisibility Rule of 36

A number is divisible by 36 if it is simultaneously divisible by both **4** (last two digits) and **9** (sum of digits).

questions.question: The expenditure and savings of a person are in ratio of 7 : 2 respectively. His savings increase by 1/3 of his income and income remains the same. What is the new respective ratio of his expenditure and savings?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio of **Expenditure** : **Savings** = 7 : 2 ⇒ **Income** = 7 + 2 = 9 units.

Increase in **Savings** = 1/3 × **Income** = 1/3 × 9 = 3 units.

Since **Income** is constant, this increase comes directly from **Expenditure**.

New **Savings** = 2 + 3 = 5 units | New **Expenditure** = 7 − 3 = 4 units.

New Ratio = 4 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of **Expenditure** to **Savings** = 7 : 2.

**Formula Used:** **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab3a4358f8f6b987d30274f7acd4ebda41686474a541871131c21fd2bd941076.png] 

Let **Expenditure** = 7x and **Savings** = 2x.

⇒ **Income** = 7x + 2x = 9x.

⇒ Increase in **Savings** = 1/3 × 9x = 3x.

⇒ New **Savings** = 2x + 3x = 5x.

⇒ New **Expenditure** = **Total Income** − New **Savings**

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 9x − 5x = 4x.

⇒ New Ratio = 4x : 5x = 4 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Concept

The fundamental relation is **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**. Any change in one component must be balanced by others if the total income is fixed.

Ratio Balancing

When a fraction of one quantity is moved to another while the total remains constant, the sum of the ratio parts does not change.

Percentage Change in Income

If **Income** increases by x%, **Expenditure** by y%, and **Savings** by z%, then: (Initial E × y%) + (Initial S × z%) = (Initial I × x%).

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Will they release the new season next month?

options.text: Will the new season be released next month?
Will the new season be release by them next month?
Will the new season be releasing next month?
Will the new season released by them next month?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the new season be released next month?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Simple Future Tense** (Active Voice).
 
• In the **Active Voice**, the structure for a **Simple Future** question is: **Will + Subject + V1 (Base Form) + Object?**
 
• To convert this into the **Passive Voice**, the grammatical formula changes to: **Will + Object (acting as Subject) + be + V3 (Past Participle) + (by + Agent)?**
 
• In this conversion, the object **the new season** shifts to the subject position, and the verb **release** is transformed into its third form, **released**.
 
• The auxiliary verb **be** must be placed before the **past participle** to complete the passive construction in the future tense.
 
• In English grammar, the agent (e.g., **by them**) is often omitted in the **Passive Voice** if the subject is a general or indefinite pronoun like **they**, **people**, or **someone**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Future Passive Rules**:
 
 
• **Affirmative Structure**: Subject + **will be** + **V3** (e.g., The season will be released).

• **Interrogative Structure**: **Will** + Subject + **be** + **V3**? (e.g., Will the season be released?).
 
 
 
• **Structural Analysis of Incorrect Options**:
 
 
• The use of the base form **release** instead of the **past participle** is a common error in passive constructions, as seen in the second option.
 
• The **Future Continuous** form (e.g., **be releasing**) denotes an ongoing action in the future and does not satisfy the requirements of a standard passive conversion for the simple future.
 
• The omission of the verb **be** in an interrogative passive sentence renders the sentence grammatically incomplete and incorrect.
 
 
</ul

• To convert this into **Passive Voice**, the **Object** of the active sentence (**my internship**) becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence.

• The structural formula for **Future Perfect** in the **Passive Voice** is: **New Subject + will have been + Past Participle (V3) + (by + agent)**.

• The auxiliary verb **been** is mandatory when converting any perfect tense (Present, Past, or Future) into its passive form to indicate the state of completion.

• Applying these rules, the verb **will have completed** is transformed into **will have been completed**.

• The adverbial phrase **By the end of the year** denotes the future time limit and remains at the beginning of the sentence to maintain the original emphasis on the deadline.

• **Incorrect Options**:

• **will have completed**: This is active voice; it implies the internship itself is performing the action.

• **has been completed**: This is **Present Perfect Passive**, which refers to an action completed in the past or very recently, not in the future.

• **will be completed**: This is **Simple Future Passive**, which does not convey the sense of an action being finished **by** a specific point in time.

</ul
